 Order

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
1. This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking the following reliefs:-
(i) That an appropriate Writ/Direction/Order be passed for issuing directions to Respondents No.1 to 4 to comply with the proper procedure and provide justice to the petitioner by conducting fair investigation against the accused and others involved.

(ii) That, an appropriate Writ/Direction/Order be passed by taking appropriate penal actions against the accused and the authoritative persons involved helping the accused and all such authoritative persons involved in the investigation must be suspended if helped the accused.
(iii) That, Any other relief which this Court may deem fit in favor of petitioner and in interests of justice.

2. The grievance of the petitioner is that on petitioner's complaint, an FIR at Crime No.13/2023 has been registered at Police Station, Agar Malwa, District Agar (M.P.) against respondent No.5 under Section 376, 452, 506 of IPC and Section 3(1)(w-i), 3(1)(w-ii), 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Caste and Yashoda Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5539524/
1 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6691 2 WP-38246-2024 Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, however, the police is not carrying out the proper investigation which has also led anticipatory bail being allowed to respondent No.5 by this Court in Criminal Appeal No.2267/2024 dated 24/08/2024, whereas the police has also filed Khatma report in the present case giving clean chit to the accused.

entities.text: Police Station, Agar Malwa, District Agar
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Yashoda Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
3. Having heard the counsel for the parties and on perusal of the documents filed on record as also the Khatma report, this Court is of the considered opinion that the petitioner shall be at liberty to take objection in respect of acceptance of the aforesaid Khatma report before the concerned Court,
and if such an objection is filed by the petitioner, the same shall be decided by the concerned Court,
in accordance with law, by a reasoned and speaking order.
It is made clear that this Court has not reflected upon the merits of the matter.
4. With the aforesaid observation, writ petition stands disposed of.
